clue.text: Undertaking expected to be successful

definitions.meaning: a pledge or vow to do something, as a noun-like gerund
showing signs of future success, as a likely talent does

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a gerund for vowing; the other is an adjective for something with bright prospects.

clue.text: Stand to set a record on unfamiliar green

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the word green is made strange, so its letters are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to set a record on a golf green they have never played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' rearranges GREEN into ERGNE, which is set on (below, in a down entry) EP.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece stand for a dining table, holding fruit or flowers.

clue.text: A soldier carrying a note needed transport

indicators.note: the soldier holds the note within him, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fighter is a soldier or warrior
RE is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A soldier with a message needs a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' signals the container; 'A' and 'needed' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo ship or aircraft, a means of carrying goods.

clue.text: Pad a convertible piece of furniture so it's really versatile

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Padding a sofa bed makes it a genuinely flexible item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a sofa bed in the surface, but it is the anagram signal for 'Pad a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something able to adjust to many uses or conditions.

clue.text: Award a mark without point

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the a-mark pair goes around the point

parts.note: a sign is a mark or symbol
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A judge gives a score, docking nothing for a lost point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: A SIGN surrounds S. 'Without point' looks like a deduction, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is to allot or give, as one would award a task or prize.

clue.text: The best advice to give viewers?

definitions.meaning: a playful instruction to people looking: gaze less often

explanation.definitionFit: One sense means matchless; the other splits into a command to look less, which suits onlookers.

clue.text: A man hoping to build a tiptop structure beginning right

parts.note: taken as written
a spire is the tall pointed top of a steeple

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word right is taken

explanation.surface: An ambitious man wants to put up a soaring tower, starting with the right approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning right' gives R, the first letter of 'right'; it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirer is someone with ambitions, one who hopes to achieve something.

clue.text: Made up stories and have to rest

parts.note: to have told lies is to have lied
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: A tired fibber invents tales and then needs a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying down is taking a rest, reclining to relax.

clue.text: Official statements concerning harbours

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
ports are harbours

explanation.surface: Bulletins are issued about the condition of the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports are formal written or spoken accounts issued by an authority.

clue.text: Marine taking direction in a career set-back

indicators.note: the reversed phrase takes the compass letter into itself
the phrase a career is turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: to career is to rush along, so career as a noun suggests speed
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A soldier changes course after a setback in his working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' turns A SPEED into DEEPSA; 'taking' puts E inside it before the final A. 'Marine' looks like a soldier but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea describes the open ocean far from shore, so it is a maritime adjective.

clue.text: Making a cocktail requires expertise in short

indicators.note: the skill sits inside the short word

parts.note: mini means very short, as in a miniskirt
art means skill or expertise

explanation.surface: A good mixed drink needs a bartender's know-how, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'short' is an adjective (as in a brief skirt), not a call to abbreviate.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a classic gin and vermouth drink served in a stemmed glass.

clue.text: Where people are questioned about their food-intake?

definitions.text: Where people are questioned about their food-intake?

parts.words: Where people are questioned about their food-intake?
parts.note: reads as an interrogation chamber, since to grill is to question hard, but describes a restaurant serving grilled food

explanation.definitionFit: A grillroom is a restaurant specialising in grilled meat, punning on grilling as interrogation.

clue.text: To break up calls for courage

explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean to analyse into components; the noun means steadfast determination.

clue.text: Composed nun — she is all brightness

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled into a new word

explanation.surface: A serene nun beams with cheerfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like calm, but rearranges NUN SHE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlight is the sun's brightness, and figuratively cheerful radiance.

clue.text: Bound to follow severe weather

definitions.meaning: the season that comes after winter's harsh conditions

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a leap; the other is the season after winter.

clue.text: Ribbon the great tsar conferred on bastard

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: Peter the Great was tsar of Russia
in its sense of not genuine or counterfeit, matching sham

explanation.surface: A ribbon of honour is bestowed by the great tsar on an illegitimate son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conferred on' puts PETER above SHAM. 'Bastard' means spurious here, not illegitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded ribbon used for hat bands and waistbands.

clue.text: Dare begin reforming, and that's material

indicators.note: the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A dare to start reforming things, and that's substantial stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges DARE BEGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaberdine is a tightly woven twill fabric, often used for raincoats.

clue.text: Object, having troublesome sore back

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

indicators.note: the word sore is made unruly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A patient protests about a painful back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' rearranges SORE into ORSE. 'back' looks like part of the body but is the verb, support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or approve, to back a candidate or plan.

clue.text: Dissent for example within a community

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the community

parts.note: a nation is a community of people

explanation.surface: There is disagreement inside a group, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' signals the container; 'Dissent' is the noun sense, a denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is denial or contradiction, a refusal to agree.

clue.text: Make a hole in about a half-hundred. That should be plenty

indicators.note: the piercing verb goes around the other letters

parts.note: to gore is to pierce with a horn
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A bull gores about fifty victims, which ought to be enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and L (Roman 50) inside GORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in abundance, always after its noun.

clue.text: Non-professional taking a degree with true potential

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: the word true is treated as having potential to become something else, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: An amateur takes a degree that shows genuine promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges TRUE into TEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for pleasure, not as a paid occupation.

clue.text: Ham on the turn

parts.note: over means on top of, as on does
a performer's act is their turn on stage

explanation.surface: A joint of meat is starting to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' reads as meat going sour; a variety performer's turn is their spot on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggerated theatricality.

clue.text: The basis of hand-cream?

parts.note: reads as a lotion's base ingredient, while also suggesting an oil for the inner surface of the hand

explanation.definitionFit: Palm oil comes from oil palm fruit and is used in cosmetics; the palm is also part of the hand.

clue.text: Some youngsters, restive, get a telling-off and become passive

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lifted out of them

explanation.surface: Fidgety kids who are scolded may go quiet and sullen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run inside 'restive, get a telling-off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vegetate is to live inactively, doing nothing stimulating.

clue.text: Fears losing head and making blunders

indicators.note: the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: terrors are fears

explanation.surface: Anxieties that lose their grip lead to mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes T from TERRORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, slips or gaffes.

clue.text: The janitor's no casual worker!

definitions.meaning: someone who takes care, the opposite of careless

explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker looks after a building, and the word splits as someone who takes care.

clue.text: Finding tot in the tall grass, carried on

indicators.note: the total goes inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall marsh grass
to tot up is to add, and a sum is a total

explanation.surface: Finding a toddler in long grass, the search party continued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. 'tot' looks like a child but means an added-up total.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to continue after a pause.

clue.text: Splendid attire and excellent drink brought back

indicators.note: the whole phrase is returned, read from its end

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: Fine clothes and a top drink are fetched back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns AILAGER into REGALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial robes and insignia, finery worn for state occasions.

clue.text: Get into a row — not for the first time

definitions.text: Get into a row — not for the first time

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to align is to bring into a straight line

explanation.surface: Someone picks yet another quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests an argument, but means a line; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to set things in line again after they have shifted.

clue.text: The ordinary quality interests odd characters

indicators.note: the letters of the word are made odd, put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: The everyday quality of life fascinates eccentrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' rearranges INTERESTS; 'characters' looks like people.
explanation.definitionFit: Triteness is being commonplace or overused, the property of the banal.
